translations.text: All who lived throughout the land rejected the command of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Persia, and did not go with him to war, because they did not fear him. In their eyes he was like an ordinary man, and his messengers returned from their presence naked and disgraced.
In the seventeenth year he fought against King Arphaxad with his army, defeated him, and brought in all his forces, all his horses, and all his chariots.
He captured Arphaxad in the region of Rages, pierced him with a spear, and destroyed him forever.
After this, when he had finished his deliberations, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Persia, summoned Holofernes, the commander of his army, who served under him.
As surely as I live and my kingdom stands firm, I will do this with my own hands, just as I have said.
He counted the chosen fighting men, as his master had commanded: 102,000 infantry and 102,000 archers.
He crossed the Euphrates, passed through Mesopotamia, and plundered all their great cities above the cities of [?], until he reached the region.
He and his army went down into their territories. He secured their great cities and took chosen men from among them to accompany them.

He went around their territories and broke their images. He had been commanded to destroy all the people's gods, so that they would worship Nebuchadnezzar alone, and all nations and all territories would call him God.

He said to them, “Tell me, people of Canaan, who are these people who live in the mountains? Who are those who live there, and how large is their army? What is their source of strength, and who is the king established over them, or their ruler, or their commander?”

But now they have returned to their God and have gathered there from the places where they were scattered. They have settled in Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and have also settled in the mountains, because the land was deserted.
But if these people have committed no offense, do not attack them, my lord, lest the Lord strengthen them and their God stand up for them, and we become a disgrace throughout all the territories.
Then, when the men around the assembly had fallen silent, Holofernes, the commander of the Assyrian army, spoke to Achior before all the foreigners and all the people of Moab.
Holofernes commanded his servants who stood before him in his tent to take Achior, send him to Bethulia, and hand him over to the Israelites.
On the next day Holofernes commanded his entire army and all his people who fought alongside him to march to Bethulia, advance into the mountain passes, and fight against the Israelites.
And now, my lord, do not fight them in open battle, and none of your people will die—not a single man.
Their children, their wives, and their young men grew weak and wasted away from thirst. They fell in the city squares and in the approaches to the gates, and they no longer had any strength.
May God judge between us and you, because you have done us a great wrong by not speaking of deliverance through peace with the Assyrians.
Even if he chooses to help us within these five days, he has the power to save us however he wishes, whether throughout all our days or to destroy us before our enemies.
But you must not try to dictate to the Lord your God, because God is not like a human being who can be coerced, nor is he like a mortal who takes offense.

She took off the sackcloth she wore and put on her widow's clothing. She washed her body with water, anointed herself with perfume, arranged the hair of her head, and adorned herself with her headdress. Then she put on the festive clothes she used to wear when her husband Manasseh was alive.
They did so, and Judith went out with her maid. The people of the city watched her until she had descended the mountain and passed through the valley, and they could no longer see her.
Holofernes said to her, “Take courage, woman, and do not let your heart be afraid, for I do not harm anyone who submits to serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of the whole world.”
If you follow the words of your servant, God will bring the undertaking to completion, and nothing of what you have planned will fail, my lord.
For their food and their supplies of water have run out, and they have begun to eat their livestock. They are determined to eat all these things that their God forbade them to eat in their law.
When I learned all this, I, your servant, withdrew from them, and God sent me to do with you a deed that, when people hear of it, will make the whole earth tremble.
They said, “From one end of the earth to the other, there is no woman like this one in the beauty of her face and the wisdom of her words.”

Holofernes said to her, “God has done well for you by sending you ahead of your people, so that you may be under the protection of our hands, while those who rebelled against my lord face death and destruction.”
Judith said to him, “As you live, my lord, your servant will not use up what she has with her before God accomplishes through my hands what he has planned.”
Holofernes’ servants brought her into a tent, and she spent the night there and slept until midnight.
She rose at that hour, and after the night watch she sent word to Holofernes, saying, “My lord, give orders that they allow your servant to go out.”
She stood over him, took hold of the hair of his head, and said, “My Lord, God of Israel, strengthen me today.”
She said to them in a loud voice, “Praise God, for he has not withdrawn his kindness and mercy from Israel, but has destroyed its enemy this night.”

“May God make your name everlasting and watch over you with his goodness, because you did not spare your own life in the face of your people’s suffering, but went out to face death and walked uprightly before our God.” And the people said, “Amen and amen.”

“Then, when morning dawns and the sun rises over the earth, all of you take your weapons of war. Let all the mighty men go outside the city, and appoint a commander for yourselves. And when you go down into the country toward the guards of the Assyrians—

“All of you take your weapons of war and carry them. When their guards see you, they will go to their camp to rouse the commanders of the Assyrian army and their forces. Then they will run to Holofernes’ tent and will not find him. Then they will be afraid and terrified and flee before you.
“But you and everyone living throughout the territory of Israel must pursue them and watch for them along all their roads.”
When Achior saw everything God had done for Israel, he believed firmly in God, was circumcised, and joined the house of Israel, where he remains to this day.
When the Assyrians saw them, they sent word to their commanders.
When no one answered him, he [?] and went into the chamber. He found his body lying on the ground, with his head no longer on it.
He went into the tent where Judith was staying and did not find her. He ran to his people, cried out to them, and said to them:
Those in the camp and those in the mountains around Bethulia also heard and fled. Then all the Israelite fighting men rose and pursued them.

When the Israelites heard, they all pursued them together and killed them as far as Choba. Those from Jerusalem and all their surrounding territories also came, because they had been told what had happened in their enemies’ camp. Those from Galilee and Gilead also pursued them and inflicted a great slaughter on them, until they had gone beyond Damascus and its territory.
The Assyrians came from the mountains to the north. Their forces came out by the thousands; their numbers blocked the rivers, and their horses’ hooves covered the rocky ground.
And the Lord, who rules over all, killed them by the hand of a woman.

For their mighty warrior did not fall by the hand of a young man, nor did the sons of the Titans kill them, nor did great giants defeat them. Instead, Judith, the daughter of Merari, weakened him with the beauty of her face.
She left her widow’s clothes upon those who were mourning in Israel.
She anointed her face with perfume, braided her hair, and [?]. She put on festive clothes to deceive him and put on her sandals.
Her beauty captivated his eyes, and her cheeks took his soul captive. The sword passed through his neck.
The Persians were startled by her daring, and the Medes were afraid of her courage.
Then my afflicted ones cried out, and my sick ones were afraid and terrified and raised their voices.
The sons of my daughters pursued them and struck them. Their young men also hurled stones at them, and they perished in the Lord’s battle.
I will proclaim praise to the Lord; I will proclaim new praise to the Lord.
The Lord is great and exceedingly glorious, and his power is astonishing.
Let all your works praise you, for you spoke and they came into being. You sent your spirit and they were formed, and there is nothing that does not obey your word.
For the foundations of the mountains shake, and the heavens also shake. The rocks melt like wild honey before your face, yet you show favor to those who fear you.
For no sacrifice is sufficient for a pleasing fragrance, and all the fat is too little for your offering. But whoever fears the Lord is great at all times.
Woe to the nations that rise against my people! The Lord, who rules over all, will take vengeance on them on the day of judgment.
He will send fire and worms into their flesh, and they will weep in pain forever.
When they reached Jerusalem, they worshiped God. After they had purified themselves, the people brought their offerings and their voluntary gifts.
Judith deposited all the possessions of Holofernes that the people had given her.
The people rejoiced in Jerusalem before the sanctuary for three months, and Judith stayed with them.
After those days, everyone returned to his own property. Judith also returned to Bethulia and lived on her estate, and throughout her life she was honored in all the land.
Many desired her, but no man had sexual relations with her throughout her life after her husband Manasseh died and was buried among his people.
She grew very old.
She grew old in the house of her husband Manasseh, reaching one hundred and [?].
The house of Israel mourned her for seven days. Before she died, she divided her possessions among all the relatives of her husband Manasseh and her own close relatives.
No one frightened the Israelites during Judith’s lifetime, nor for many days after she died.
